Stereoselective rhodium-catalyzed reaction
of allenes with organoboronic reagents for
diversiﬁed branched 1,3-alkadienes
Weiyi Wang 1, Shichao Hong1,W e n x i a n gH e1, Xue Zhang 2 ,H u iQ i a n 1 &
Shengming Ma 1,2
The terminal isoprene unit, as the simplest branched 1,3-diene unit, exists in a
wide range of natural products and bioactive molecules. Herein, we report a
stereoselective rhodium-catalyzed reaction of allenes with readily available
methyl pinacol boronic ester, providing a straightforward approach to iso-
prene derivatives with a very high E-stereoselectivity. Its synthetic potential
has been illustrated by a concise synthesis of natural product schinitrienin.
Such a protocol can be easily extended to aryl and alkenyl boronic reagents
affording 2-aryl or -alkenyl substituted 1,3-dienes, which are also of high
importance in organic synthesis but remain challenging for their selective
synthesis, with a remarkable stereoselectivity. A series of deuterium-labeling
experiments indicate a unique mechanism, which involves reversibleβ-H
elimination as well as hydrometalation and isomerization of the allylic rho-
dium species.
The terminal isoprene unit, as an iconic type of 1,3-dienes, exists in a
wide range of natural products and bioactive molecules (Fig. 1a)1– 6.
Featured by the methyl group on the 2-position, the terminal isoprene
unit is the simplest branched 1,3-diene unit. However, although the
synthesis of linear 1,3-dienes has been well-developed, the stereo-
selective synthetic methods for branched 1,3-dienes are still very
limited
7– 9. Allenes have been developed as versatile synthetic building
blocks for the synthesis of various types of ole ﬁns due to the unique
and diverse reactivity of their two cumulated carbon-carbon double
bonds
10– 18. Branched 1,3-dienes can be synthesized from α-functiona-
lized allenes and aryl/alkenyl metallic species, which requires pre-
installation of a leaving group in allene (Fig. 1b)
19– 32.F o rc o m m o n
allenes without a leaving group, the carbometalation of allenes with
organometallic species would generate alkenyl metallic species or
allylic metallic species
14,a n dt h e β-H elimination of allylic metallic
species would, in principle, afford the targeted branched 1,3-dienes
(Fig. 1c). Previously reported oxidative addition of aryl/alkenyl halides
with Pd(0)
33– 38 and aryl/alkenyl C– H activation applying the directing
group39,40, are all not applicable for the methylation to form the
terminal isoprene unit existing in numerous natural products as shown
in Fig. 1a. We envisioned that a strategy of transmetalation of readily
commercially available organoboronic reagents with a proper metal
catalyst may address the issues for the efﬁcient synthesis of branched
1,3-dienes from allenes: (1) achieving the desired methylation for nat-
ural product syntheses; (2) mild conditions, thus, resulting in a very
promising selectivity. Herein, we report a Rh-catalyzed reaction of
allenes with organoboronic reagents, using a copper salt as the coca-
talyst with air as the green oxidant to complete the catalytic cycle,
affording branched 1,3-dienes with a high stereoselectivity and a broad
substrate scope under very mild conditions (Fig.1d). Methylation has
been realized and successfully applied to the concise synthesis of
natural product schinitrienin.

To our delight, this protocol may also be readily extended to the
synthesis of 2-aryl or -alkenyl substituted 1,3-dienes by using aryl or
alkenyl boronic reagents (Fig. 3). The reactivity is much higher since

reactions of monosubstituted allenes with various organoboronic
reagents (Fig. 3a), affording 2-substituted 1,3-dienes. Both pinacol
boronic esters (Method B) and boronic acids (Method C) could be
applied and the generality of pinacol boronic esters is better. Both
electron-rich and electron-deﬁcient aryl pinacol boronic esters reacted
with allenes in high yields. Importantly, a variety of synthetically ver-

E-3fq, E-3cs), protected hydroxy ( E-3hb), protected amines ( E-3kb,

E-3ai, E-3aj, E-3ak, E-3aab, E-3aac, E-3at, E-3au), bromo (E-3ag,
E-3ah),

The high stereoselectivity of the reaction of 1,3-disubstituted
allenes could be attributed to the steric effect: The π-σ-π rearrange-
ment from η3-(syn,anti)-G1 to η3-(anti,anti)-G2 is disfavored due to the
large allylic 1,3-strain as well as the closer distance between Ar2 and the
Rh-Cp* moiety65,66. Based on the information shown in Fig. 7a, there
should be another type of allylic Rh intermediateη3-(syn,syn)-H1,w h i c h
would isomerize to η3-(syn,syn)-H2 via the C – C bond rotation, how-
ever, due to the increased allylic 1,3-strain 65,66, such isomerization is
also disfavored. Overall, the formation of (1E,3E)-stereoisomers would
be disfavored (Fig. 7b).

(for more detailed information, see Supplementary Information and
Supplementary Data 1). The displayed energies are Gibbs free energies
incorporating the solvent effect of THF. The transmetalation of

boronic reagents has been developed, affording diversi ﬁed bran-
ched 1,3-dienes in an excellent stereoselectivity under very mild
reaction conditions, enjoying a very broad substrate scope and
tolerating a large variety of functional groups. The reaction uses
Cu(OAc)
2·H2O as a cocatalyst with the assistance of oxygen from air
as the green oxidant to complete the catalytic cycle. Methylation
has been achieved by this protocol and the synthetic practicability
has been illustrated by the concise synthesis of natural product
schinitrienin. A mechanism has been proposed involving reversible
β-H elimination as well as hydrometalation and isomerization of the
allylic rhodium species. Further studies are currently ongoing in our
laboratory.
